newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice mixed, China sale to Manila watched.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice mixed, China sale to Manila watched.

text.p: Thai rice prices were mostly mixed this week on slow demand but fragrant rice values surged on dwindling supplies and active short-covering, trade sources said on Thursday.
Traders also watched keenly the recent China sale of 200,000 tonnes of rice to Philippines as it raised ideas whether the Chinese could become a serious competitor to Thai exporters.
The benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around $355-385 per tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $360-390 tonne a week earlier.
The 100 fragrant rice, on the other hand, rose sharply to $650-670 per tonne on the same basis from $620-630 last week.
There was a market talk that the fragrant rice price was pushed up partly by Malaysian buying through a recent tender. The details of the purchase were not available.
Traders said most buyers might stay out of Thai market for a while in anticipation that the prices would ease once more supplies from a second crop rice hit the market in March.
"The fragrant rice shot up because of heavy demand to meet obligations, especially to Hong Kong, but the supplies in the market were limited," said one rice trader from a major house.
"Otherwise, the market was rather quiet with small buying here and there. We expected more buying to emerge in March when the prices dropped from current levels," he added.
The market was also divided in its interpretation of the China rice sale to Manila.
Some shrugged off the report, saying it would take a while until net rice importer China would emerge as an export competitor.
One trader said China might even have to import rice from Thailand to meet the obligations.
"I don't see this as a threat. My opinion is it will take a while before China will become a major rice exporter," the trader said.
"This year, for example, the industry estimated that China might need to import as much as a million tonnes," he said.
But others suggested the the move could have reflected a trend that Thailand could not afford to ignore.
"If you look at their rice import-export figures in the past year, you will see that the rice export growth has jumped while imports had dropped," said an exporter.
China rice exports in 1996 reached 260,000 tonnes, a 465.9 percent increase from 1995 while the rice imports of the same year fell 53.6 percent to 760,000 tonnes from the year earlier.
